notice: New English editing pass, not restoration of the lost production translation. Each entry contains paragraph number, replacement, and rationale. Semantic questions remain in qa/chapter-0001.json.
edits: The years of bloodshed had finally ended.
Add missing terminal punctuation.
The war between humans and demons had lasted for decades, leaving a terrifying record in the history books as the ‘Age of Destruction’.
Repair narrative tense and clause structure; retain the named era.
And then came the day when humanity’s victory was written down in the books.
Repair the fragment and narrative tense without changing the chronology.
Vikir struggled.
Add missing terminal punctuation.
A bastard. The son of a concubine.
Fix capitalization and article; preserve the rhetorical fragments.
That was why his middle name was ‘Van’.
Supply the missing predicate; spelling remains provisional.
He had not been born with a surname such as ‘Le’ or ‘Re’, which his half-siblings in the main family received. Because of that, he had to work hundreds of times harder than others.
Repair tense and comparative wording; retain source surname terminology pending review.
But in the end, it was all for nothing.
Add introductory comma.
Spying, assassination, kidnapping, blackmail, smuggling… For the sake of his family, he had carried out more than 500 dangerous missions, but in the end, they forsook him.
Repair mission collocation, tense, and punctuation; preserve quantity and activities.
He was falsely accused of being a spy for the demons and executed.
Repair the fragment and redundant false-charge wording using the recovered English claim; accusation needs source review.
He wanted to live.
Add missing terminal punctuation.
It was a harsh first assessment for a father to make of his children born that year.
Repair English clause order and temporal reference.
… At that moment.
Normalize ellipsis; retain transition as a deliberate fragment.
As Hugo passed the cribs in the nursery, he stopped at one of them.
Repair awkward location wording using the cribs already named.
Hugo looked at Vikir, and his expression softened a little.
Use idiomatic wording for the stated change in expression.
It was not because he was pleased that Vikir’s qualities seemed superior to those of his other offspring.
Repair tense; preserve the denial rather than asserting superiority.
He merely thought that if all he had before him was garbage anyway, it would be better to have garbage that was a little less noisy.
Repair clause structure while retaining Hugo’s contempt and comparison.
From the cradle to the grave.
Supply missing article.
The baby is trapped in the maze of blades and wanders through it.
Use consistent present tense for the general description and plural blades.
Every movement leaves the baby with cuts from the blades.
Repair subject and verb agreement without alternating pronouns.
If one baby absorbs most of the river’s power, another receives relatively less because less power remains.
Replace the inconsistent river pronoun and repair comparison; preserve finite power distribution.
Who would be the first to escape this labyrinth and jump into the river? That would determine the future of these children.
Remove duplicated first and align narration with past tense.
Thirty-two children born that year, including all of the family’s rightful sons, bastards, and cousins, competed in the middle of the cradle of swords.
Align narrative tense; preserve participants and number.

One baby cried for a babysitter. Another was already crawling, bleeding from cuts inflicted by the blades. Another sat sucking his finger, showing no intention of escaping yet… Babies are usually like that.
Repair subject coordination and verb forms; preserve all three described responses.
In fact, since these babies were less than a year old, this was only natural.
Repair narrative tense and literal result phrasing.
Even his own children were no exception.
Remove accidental second-person shift in narration.
“Only like this can we fight the demons. The strong will survive and leave the weak behind.”
Add quotation punctuation only; the disputed speech remains unchanged in meaning.
If the river’s power had not worked only on children under the age of one, Hugo would have soaked himself in it right away.
Repair the conditional while preserving the stated age restriction.
Hugo was looking at the river with a sad expression.
Repair incomplete temporal clause.
“Ah, how can that be!”
Repair English exclamation.
And at that moment…
Repair transition wording and signal the continuing sentence.
Through this thick forest of blades, a child was heading straight for the River Styx.
Remove unnecessary conjunction and clarify clause punctuation.
The child’s body was already covered in blood.
Align narrative tense.
Instead of following the relatively safe path around and around, he squeezed directly into the small gaps between the blades.
Repair narrative tense and idiom; retain the contrast between routes.
His knees were bruised, and his soft palms were already bloody.
Repair article and possessive consistency.
The child crawled forward, leaving a bloody path as he squeezed between the countless needles.
Supply a finite verb; retain the source needle metaphor.
His siblings were still trapped in the center of the cradle of the sword, unable to get out.
Reduce redundant clause without changing the stated location.
As soon as the child emerged from the cradle, he threw himself into the River Styx.
Repair missing conjunction and comma splice.
They had never seen him so agitated; he usually showed no emotion in anything he did.
Remove accidental first-person narration; they refers to the attendants in paragraph 98.
The child who had fallen into the River Styx still had not surfaced.
Repair narrative tense and water-specific wording.
The knights were immediately frightened.
Repair orphaned conjunction and adverb placement.
